summary: Allis State Park summit tower in Brookfield, VT: 1932 wooden lookout burned 1947-48; steel tower (1956 per state, 1966 per NRHP) still standing; restored 2025.

facts.design: Present tower: skeleton steel tower with enclosed cab and hip roof, about 50 ft to the cab floor (NRHP). Original 1932 tower: 40 ft wooden tower with glass-enclosed top.
facts.agency: Vermont Department of Forests, Parks and Recreation

access.note: Tower is inside Allis State Park, a state park. No current climbing rules or closure notice found in sources read; the 2025 work is not confirmed as closing the tower to visitors.

events.note: Wooden 40 ft tower with glass-enclosed top, completed November 1932 (newspaper accounts quoted by Forest Lookouts). NRHP gives 1933 for the original tower.
State rebuilt the cab, repaired the telephone line and prepared the station for a lookout watchman; lightning damaged part of the wooden cab and CCC crews repaired it.
Hurricane tipped the tower onto two legs; guy cables kept it from falling; damage repaired as well as possible (state report to June 1940).
Wooden tower struck by lightning and destroyed by the resulting fire (state biennial report covering 1947 to 1948; exact date not given).
New tower completed with a steel tower base and a wooden cab on top (same 1947 to 1948 report; exact date not given).
Wooden tower razed because of its unsafe condition.
Steel tower from Gilson Mountain erected in the wooden tower's place, spring 1956 (state report).
NRHP nomination says the present steel tower was built in 1966 by a private organization and replaced an original wooden tower built in 1933. Conflicts with the 1956 state record.

A $450,000 grant was being used for fencing, metal grates on wooden stairs, an interior railing and lightning grounding, with work starting on Burke Mountain and Bear Hill (WCAX, May 2025). A 2025 Vermont report says maintenance at Okemo, Burke and Bear Hill included lightning protection, paint, interior cab railings and wire mesh on stairs and landings.

corrections.why: 12.2 m (40 ft) is the height of the original 1932 wooden tower. The 2025 article gives the present tower as 48 ft.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Newspaper accounts quoted by Forest Lookouts say the state completed the tower in November 1932. The NRHP nomination gives 1933. We use 1932 for completion and note the NRHP date.

notes_for_editor: Steel tower date is unresolved: the state record says a steel tower from Gilson Mountain went up in spring 1956, while the NRHP nomination says a private organization built the present tower in 1966. A geocaching page also says 1966 but is not used. Brief corrections: height (12.2 m is the 1932 wooden tower; 48 ft now) and the 2019 event, which no source read supports. Access: the park is a state park, but no climbing rules or closure notice were found, so the access level is a judgment. The 2025 closure dates appeared only in search snippets and are not used. The NRHP title is taken from the nomination header. Used 2 WebSearch calls and 6 page reads.
